disagreements: Box depth: mine 1086 +- 33 ppm (3.5 h box, transit-masked re-detrend) vs pipeline 1023 ppm (3.75 h box). Evaluating my masked-detrend fold with the pipeline's 3.75 h box gives 1027 ppm, so the 63 ppm gap is entirely box width (ingress/egress dilution of the box mean), not data. Full trapezoid depth is 1141 ppm (pipeline TLS 1189 ppm).

Empirical noise/SNR: my random-phase-box error is 33 ppm (close to the 30 ppm formal white-noise error) giving empirical SNR 33.0; the pipeline's box_noise is 51 ppm giving SNR 20.0. I could not see how box_noise is defined (pipeline code not read); the pipeline's figure is the more conservative one and should be the quoted SNR. Both are far above any threshold.

SDE is not the same statistic: my 81.8 is the SDE of the astropy BLS log-likelihood power (a skewed statistic; SDE of the depth/depth_err spectrum is 31.4), the pipeline's 13.7 is a TLS SDE. Not comparable, not a disagreement.

Period: my BLS 15.113718 d vs pipeline 15.1136115 d (diff 1.07e-4 d). Box-likelihood periods are jagged at this level; a weighted linear ephemeris to 77 template-timed events gives P = 15.113691 +- 9.5e-5 d (errors scaled by sqrt(red-chi2)), with the pipeline at -0.8 sigma and mine at +0.3 sigma. Predicted mid-transit times differ by <= 15 min anywhere in the baseline.

Duration: my best box 3.5 h vs pipeline 3.75 h (0.25 h grid); my trapezoid T14 = 4.0 h, T23/T14 = 0.70 (TLS gave 3.1 h). T14 of 4.0 h includes ~0.5 h of 30-min-cadence smearing; the intrinsic ~3.5 h sits at the circular, b=0 maximum (3.45 h for R*=0.66 Rsun, M*=0.7 Msun), i.e. the transit must be near-central or the star slightly less dense than the catalogue estimate (same conclusion as the pipeline's duration_ratio 1.05).
Odd/even: mine 0.23 sigma vs pipeline 0.03 sigma; both null, different box widths and error estimators.

Inverted-flux null on my BLIND detrend peaked at the transit period (SDE 17.8, 185 ppm) - this is a running-median artefact (+150-250 ppm shoulders within +-12 h of each transit, visible in pass-1 fold), not an astrophysical anti-transit; it vanishes after the transit-masked re-detrend (post-hoc null: SDE 10.9 at 1.16 d, unrelated). Any un-masked detrend on a signal this strong will produce such a null peak; worth noting for how the stage-1 inverted null is interpreted.

Per-event template timings scatter 30 min rms against ~12 min delta-chi2=1 errors (chi2 528/75). I attribute this to under-estimated per-event errors at 30-min cadence (ingress ~1 cadence), not to TTVs; no TTV claim is made.
sap_vs_psf_depth: PSF FLUX depth 1086 +- 33 ppm; SAP_FLUX depth 995 +- 38 ppm at the same ephemeris and box (both transit-masked 1-d running-median detrend, empirical errors from random-phase boxes). Ratio SAP/PSF = 0.92 +- 0.04. For a signal on the target, SAP depth should be ~CROWDSAP x PSF depth = 0.885 x 1086 = 961 ppm; the measured 995 ppm is 0.9 sigma above that, i.e. consistent. A signal on a contaminant would make the aperture depth larger than the deblended PSF depth (ratio > 1); ratio 0.92 +- 0.045 disfavours that at ~1.9 sigma. Mild support for on-target, but it is not a localisation test; the pixel-level deficit centroid (pipeline pixel.json: median target-to-deficit 1.1 arcsec, deficit closer to the target than any other Gaia source in 12/13 quarters) carries that burden.

## Independent re-derivation: kic-006699887 (KIC 6699887, Gaia DR3 2077554781499350144)

All numbers below come from `/home/user/ZyushgPlanet/runs/poolA_main/adversarial/kic-006699887/rederive/results.json` (and `compare.json`, `ephemeris.json`), produced by `rederive_kic006699887.py` written from scratch with numpy/pandas/astropy. No code under `pipeline/` was imported or read; `vet.json`/`pixel.json`/`events.csv` were opened only after my numbers were written. Candidate language only: this is a first-screen signal that has passed stage 2 and pixel localisation; nothing here is a planet.

### 1. Data and detrending (own code)
- Cached KBONUS-BKG FITS, extension `LIGHTCURVE_STITCHED`, `SAP_QUALITY == 0`, finite flux: 60,219 cadences, Q1-Q17, baseline 1459.5 d; 60,087 kept after dropping positive 4-sigma outliers.
- Per quarter: divide by median, then by a centred 1.0-d time-based running median (pandas rolling). Point scatter 687 ppm (MAD), 722 ppm (std).
- Two passes. **Pass 1** is the blind detrend used for the search. **Pass 2** re-detrends with cadences within +-1 duration of each transit excluded from the trend. Pass 1 shows +150-250 ppm shoulders within +-12 h of transit (the running median sits low when the window contains the 3.8 h dip); these bias the pass-1 box depth low (937 ppm) and produce a spurious inverted-flux peak at the transit period. Headline numbers are pass 2.

### 2. Blind BLS 1-50 d (astropy BoxLeastSquares, own grid)
- Log-uniform grid, dlnP = (2 h)/(3 x baseline): 205,544 periods; durations 1.5-8 h; likelihood objective; 90 s.
- **Top peak 15.11368 d** (power 472.6, depth 997 ppm at 3.0 h box, depth-SNR 30.6). Peak 2: 30.2273 d (= 2P). Peak 3: 7.5569 d (= P/2). **The pipeline's 15.11360 d is recovered blind, as the top peak, not an alias.**
- SDE of the log-likelihood power spectrum: 81.8 (skewed statistic; SDE of the depth/depth_err spectrum is 31.4). Not comparable to the pipeline's TLS SDE 13.7.
- Inverted-flux null (2-f), same grid, pass-1 detrend: SDE 17.8 at 15.1122 d, depth 185 ppm, max power 44.6 vs 472.6 real. This IS at the transit period, but it is a detrending artefact (the shoulders above); on the transit-masked detrend the inverted null drops to SDE 10.9 at 1.163 d (unrelated), with power 11.5 at the transit period. Labelled post-hoc because the mask uses the ephemeris.

### 3. Measurements at the best ephemeris (pass 2)
| quantity | re-derived | pipeline vet.json |
|---|---|---|
| P [d] | 15.113718 (BLS); 15.113691 +- 0.000095 (timing fit) | 15.1136115 (BLS), 15.113706 (TLS) |

| box depth [ppm] | 1086 +- 33 (3.5 h box); **1027 with a 3.75 h box** | 1023 +- 33 formal |
| empirical error [ppm] / SNR | 33 (std of 3000 random-phase boxes) / **33.0** | 51 (box_noise) / 20.0 |

| transits with >= 50% coverage | **86** (of 97 epochs in the baseline) | 86 |
| per-event depths | weighted mean 1094 ppm; chi2 160/85; 79/86 events individually > 2 sigma; deepest 2388 +- 327 ppm (epoch 19, Q4), removing it leaves 1072 ppm; single-event dominance 3.5% | weighted mean 1069, chi2 152/85 |
| per-event match with pipeline events.csv | 86/86 epochs matched, Pearson r = 0.89, mean offset +25 ppm, mid-times within 13 min | |

Depth-vs-box-width scan (pass 2): 3.0 h 1126 ppm, 3.5 h 1086, 3.75 h 1027, 4.0 h 965. Trapezoid full depth 1141 ppm gives Rp/R* = 0.034, i.e. ~2.4 R_earth for R* = 0.66 Rsun with no dilution correction (pipeline 2.3). The random-box distribution never reaches the transit depth (0/3000).

Transit timing: trapezoid-template times for all 86 events, linear fit to the 77 with delta-chi2 > 4: P = 15.113691 +- 3.6e-5 d (formal), +- 9.5e-5 d after scaling by sqrt(red-chi2 = 7.0); rms residual 30 min vs median per-event error 12.5 min. I read the excess scatter as under-estimated per-event errors at 30-min cadence, not TTVs.

### 4. SAP_FLUX vs PSF FLUX (dilution check)
Same ephemeris, same box, same masked detrend: SAP depth 995 +- 38 ppm vs PSF 1086 +- 33 ppm, ratio 0.92 +- 0.04. Expected for an on-target signal: ~CROWDSAP x PSF = 0.885 x 1086 = 961 ppm (0.9 sigma away). A contaminant origin would push the aperture depth above the deblended PSF depth (ratio > 1), disfavoured at ~1.9 sigma. Supportive but weak; localisation rests on the pixel-level work (pipeline pixel.json: median target-to-deficit 1.1 arcsec, deficit closer to the target than any other Gaia source in 12/13 quarters, Gaussian-at-target beats scaled image in 13/13).

### 5. Verdict
The signal is reproduced independently in every respect that matters: blind top peak at the same period, 86 transits, flat-bottomed (T23/T14 ~0.7), depth stable across four years (chi2 3.7/3) and odd/even (0.23 sigma), no secondary (-1.1 sigma), no single-event dominance, SAP depth consistent with the on-target expectation. The only numerical differences are definitional: box width (3.5 vs 3.75 h) explains the 1086 vs 1023 ppm depth, and the empirical-noise estimator explains SNR 33 vs 20 (quote the pipeline's more conservative 20). Two items for the red team: (i) the intrinsic duration (~3.5 h after removing ~0.5 h cadence smearing) sits at the circular b=0 maximum for the catalogue R*/M*, so either a near-central transit or a slightly lower-density host is required; (ii) any detrend that does not mask transits produces an inverted-flux peak at the transit period on a signal this strong, which should be kept in mind when interpreting the stage-1 inverted null for strong detections.
